notes: rev 8 (build 55): HALO / MILITARY FREE FALL PARACHUTE DUTY CORRECTED, 225 to 240. The superseded figure was 225, sourced to 'DoD FMR Vol 7A Ch 24 para 3.3.2 (June 2025 ed.)' — that edition is superseded and our copy of it was simply old. DFAS's current published page (updated 5 March 2026) prints 240 for the Military Free Fall row, and the ruling (DECISIONS.md D-17) is that where our source is a superseded FMR edition and DFAS's current page is later, the DFAS page is sufficient authority. This is NOT a general licence: two current sources disagreeing, or DFAS against a current FMR edition, still escalates to the user. MEMBER-VISIBLE: hdipParachuteHalo is an extra-pay category on the Pay screen, so a member on military free-fall status was planning against 15/mo — 180/yr — LESS contribution room than DFAS publishes. The correction gives them more room, not less. Found by tool/verify_dfas.dart comparing every shipped figure against the captured DFAS pages; 271 others matched exactly. NOT corrected in the same pass and deliberately still absent: DFAS also publishes an Army-specific static-line rate effective Oct 1 2025 to May 20 2029 which this file does not carry — see EXTERNAL-DATA-REGISTER.md, it is a schema/shape change (branch- and date-aware rates) rather than a transcription, and it is knowingly deferred rather than undiscovered. rev 7 (v57 SS3): basicPayCapMonthly RENAMED to basicPayCapO7AndAboveMonthly. Value, official flag and source are all unchanged — this is a naming correction only. The old name read as a single universal ceiling on basic pay; there are two, and this one binds O-7 through O-10 (Executive Schedule Level II) while basicPayCapO6AndBelowMonthly binds O-6 and below (Level V). A name that hides which grades a ceiling applies to is how the wrong one gets used. Neither is ever scaled by projectedRaisePct. rev 6 (v56 SS2, audit D-19): CATCH-UP CORRECTION. catchUp50 was 7500 flagged official:false — an estimate carried over from the prototype and never verified. The real CY2026 figure is 8000, transcribed from IRS Notice 2025-67 (issued 13 November 2025, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/n-25-67.pdf; summary IR-2025-111 at https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/401k-limit-increases-to-24500-for-2026-ira-limit-increases-to-7500, which states the age-50 catch-up is increased — to the figure now carried in limits.catchUp50, cited in sources). A member aged 50+ planning against the old estimate left tax-advantaged room unused each year, silently and unrecoverably after 31 December — the shortfall being the difference between the two figures, both of which are in limits and in the verification record rather than restated here. catchUp60to63 is unchanged — the same notice states this higher limit remains at its prior value — and is now flagged official:true, which it always should have been. NOTE FOR ANYONE TEMPTED BY THE STATUTE: the super catch-up is defined as the greater of a fixed statutory floor or 150% of the standard catch-up — and computing 150% of the current standard catch-up does NOT reproduce the published super catch-up. The two disagree. Transcribe, never derive; the published figures are in limits. Transcribe, never derive. rev 5 (v52-3): sgli block added — the VA-published SGLI premium table, transcribed verbatim from https://www.va.gov/life-insurance/options-eligibility/sgli/ (page states last updated 2025-09-19), carried as printed rather than derived from the rate; validation rejects any level that disagrees with the stated rate. rev 4 (v45 SS2): basicPayCapMonthly added — the statutory ceiling on monthly basic pay, 37 U.S.C. 203(a)(2) (O-7 through O-10 basic pay limited to Executive Schedule Level II). the CY2026 monthly figure as printed in the official DFAS 2026 basic pay table, whose capped O-9/O-10 rows are already transcribed in this file's payTable — the key restates that in-file official figure with its rule, and the figure itself lives in basicPayCapO7AndAboveMonthly rather than being repeated here. rev 3: axisDateLabel on the AvIP byYears tables (v25 SS4, additive). 3.8% raise per NDAA FY26; limits per IRS Notice 2025-67.

sgli.source: VA, "Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance (SGLI)", https://www.va.gov/life-insurance/options-eligibility/sgli/ — premium rate table transcribed verbatim; page states "Last updated: September 19, 2025". Coverage is offered to $500,000 in $50,000 increments at 5 cents per $1,000 per month, plus $1.00 per month for Traumatic Injury Protection (TSGLI). VERIFIED FIRST-PARTY 2026-08-06 (v57 §9.1): va.gov answered 200 — it is not DFAS and does not refuse scripted requests — and the page was captured to cowork/reference/va-2026/sgli.html, sha256 bc63e9e343e1194c28fb068caa30b72a833b192e221135ba21c15b441eda9415. All ten coverage levels, the 0.05 per-$1,000 rate, the $1.00 TSGLI charge and the 2025-09-19 date match the live page exactly. The prior 'Cowork to verify' clause is discharged.
